investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC, escalated once to Level 2 STRUCTURAL after Level 1 was genuinely insufficient. A plain curl GET of the official /en/events/ page returns a client-rendered shell (a loading spinner, no server-rendered event cards) — Level 1 could not directly expose event data. Inspecting the page's own linked JS bundles (retained under evidence/) revealed a bespoke first-party WordPress plugin ('auditori-plugin') whose own eventsarchive.js calls a documented internal helper (get_query(), in helper.js) that issues a plain GET against the site's own admin-ajax.php with action=get_auditori_events_query — a plain, unauthenticated curl GET against that exact URL then returned real, structured event JSON directly (Level 2, no browser/headless step needed).

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://www.auditori.cat/en/events/ returns only a client-rendered shell (a-events-container/a-loading elements, no server-rendered event cards, no JSON-LD Event/MusicEvent blocks) — no event data is present in the raw HTML itself.

Inspecting the page's own linked first-party JS (auditori-plugin's eventsarchive.js + helper.js, both retained) revealed a documented internal AJAX helper calling admin-ajax.php?action=get_auditori_events_query. A plain, unauthenticated curl GET against that exact URL (with the same X-Requested-With/Referer headers the site's own JS sends) returned real, structured event JSON directly — no browser/headless observation was needed to discover this data path.

venue_reference: L'Auditori de Barcelona (main venue, Carrer de Lepant 150) plus its own touring/community programme and Early Music cycle, which its own feed cross-lists at several OTHER real, distinct, independently canonical Barcelona venues (see 'Cross-listed venues' below) — matching this project's existing Jamboree->Paral-lel-62 cross-listing precedent, never merged into one venue.

identity.notes: Official identity confirmed directly from the retained evidence at https://www.auditori.cat/.

site_classification.platform: WordPress with a bespoke first-party plugin ('auditori-plugin') exposing its own custom admin-ajax.php action — not the standard Tribe Events Calendar plugin.

title.notes: Each record's own 'wp_post.post_title' (HTML-entity-decoded by this package's collector), combined with 'subtitle' when present.

start_date.notes: Each record's own 'event_next_date', a genuine Unix-seconds timestamp — independently cross-checked against the SAME record's own human-readable 'event_date_text' for several sampled records (e.g. unix 1788627600 == 'September 5, 2026 · 7 p.m.' local Europe/Madrid CEST) — a real UTC instant, not a floating/local value.

time.notes: Embedded in the same 'event_next_date' unix timestamp (see start_date).

venue_location.notes: Each record's own 'hall_obj.wp_post.post_title'. This source is genuinely multi-venue (see 'Cross-listed venues' below) — resolution keys on this exact hall-name text via venues/source-venue-mappings.json's VENUE_NAME-keyed entries, one per real hall, never a fuzzy match.

source_record_id.notes: Each record's own numeric 'id' (the WordPress post ID) — a stable, source-native identifier.

price.notes: Each record's own 'price_text' field, free text (e.g. '20 €', 'Free Admission', 'To determinate').

reasons: acquisition_class EMBEDDED_JSON, a resolved supported class.
A CONFIRMED public data path retained (239 real records observed live across the site's own from_date-cursor pagination, ~152 music-programme-filtered at proof time).

title and start_date both PROVEN, directly stated by the source (the start_date's UTC-instant reading independently cross-checked against the source's own parallel human-readable text field, not asserted on faith).
source_record_id PROVEN via the source's own numeric WordPress post ID.
recommended_family NEW_FAMILY_REQUIRED — a bespoke, venue-specific implementation for a non-generalisable first-party plugin, matching this project's existing bespoke-collector precedent.

evidence.description: The official /en/events/ page's own raw, unauthenticated HTML response — a client-rendered shell, no event data present.
evidence.method: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser)

evidence.description: The first-party 'auditori-plugin' JS bundle (eventsarchive.js) that documents this source's own internal query mechanism, including its real pagination cursor field ('from_date').
evidence.method: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser)

evidence.description: The first-party helper.js, whose get_query() function documents the exact admin-ajax.php request shape (action, page, limit, from_date, etc.).
evidence.method: curl (plain HTTP GET, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication, no browser)

evidence.description: The full, live first-page response of this source's own admin-ajax.php event query — 30 real records.

evidence.description: A second, real live page of the same query using the from_date cursor derived from ev-batch-1's own max event_next_date — directly proves the site's real pagination mechanism (page alone does not advance; from_date does).
evidence.method: curl (plain HTTP GET, same headers as ev-batch-1)

evidence.description: The full, live, deduplicated result of following this source's own from_date cursor across 8 real batches (239 unique records) — the same bounded, single-window acquisition this package's own collector performs.
evidence.method: curl (plain HTTP GET, same headers as ev-batch-1, repeated with the site's own from_date cursor)

evidence.description: This package's own offline test suite (tests/auditori-barcelona.test.mjs) re-parses the retained evidence above with the actual collector code (ingestion/auditori-barcelona/discovery.mjs, ingestion/auditori-barcelona/observation-adapter.mjs) and asserts the exact fields recorded above, including the real cursor-pagination mechanism (via an injected mock fetchImpl over the two real retained batches, never a live network call) and the music-category filter's real inclusion/exclusion outcomes.
